historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Non-ergot dopamine receptor agonists

starting.description: Known dopamine-receptor agonist effects of ergot/ergoline drugs stimulated the developers to examine simpler indolone compounds. An active 7-hydroxy indolone with dopamine-like cardiovascular effects was prior art and was used as starting material in one route to the des-hydroxy compound. Separately, apomorphine's observed animal motor effects informed early Parkinson's research.

inspiration.description: Observed effects of known ergot/ergoline-derived dopamine agonists motivated the indolone program, while dopamine's cardiovascular activity and that of a dopamine-mimicking 7-hydroxy indolone supplied physiological and pharmacological reference points. An independent apomorphine branch followed observed animal motor effects. Ergot agents are historical inspirations, not members of the assigned class.

steps.description: Researchers observed dopamine-receptor agonism among existing ergot/ergoline compounds and used those working effects as a starting clue for a simpler peripheral D2 agonist.
The 7-hydroxy indolone series showed reported dopamine-like cardiovascular effects; its di-n-propyl congener was developed as an active predecessor.

Chemists prepared and tested des-hydroxy indolones, including the compound later called ropinirole; the inventor used the active 7-hydroxy congener in one route and reported retained D2 and cardiovascular effects.

The same indolone compound was subsequently investigated for Parkinson's disease, as documented by an early small open clinical study; the reason and timing of the therapeutic shift are not established here.

In a separate earlier branch, apomorphine's observed effects on animal movement helped motivate clinical investigation in Parkinson's disease; the 1951 clinical observations predated the later dopamine-receptor explanation.

design.description: The team hypothesized an active ergoline fragment, designed and tested simpler indolones without the full ergot or catechol framework, and prepared a des-hydroxy compound with reported D2 activity. The work created and evaluated a changed molecular architecture for a selective pharmacological goal, not merely a delivery formulation.

circumstances.description: The named event is the deliberate synthesis and pharmacological testing of indolones as selective peripheral D2 agonists; this does not assert that every result was expected or that the earlier biological clues were planned.

limits: The documented development route applies to the ropinirole indolone branch; other chemically distinct non-ergot dopamine-agonist lineages cannot be assumed to have the same founding history.
The independently developed apomorphine branch is summarized from a historical review; no direct parentage to ropinirole is claimed.
Ergot/ergoline drugs were inspiration, not cohort members or the final non-ergot architecture.
The original developers described a cardiovascular program, not an initially Parkinson-specific discovery program.
The retrospective dopamine-analogue depiction (E5) and the developers' stated ergoline-activity stimulus (E1) emphasize different aspects; structural analogy alone does not establish motivation.
gaps: The 1985 ropinirole-specific journal report was read only as an abstract; the 1986 primary research and patent passages were read.
The 1951 Schwab apomorphine report was located by PMID 14913646 but not read; the separate branch is supported by a historical review.
The sources read do not establish the reason or exact timing of the indolone program's shift from cardiovascular research to Parkinson's disease.
